A marker is where they read to, never when.

payload.invalid-examples.json of https://trusttasks.org/spec/rooms/owner/group/remove/0.1: (1) No member. Removal names whom it removes; a recipient asked to choose would be deciding who leaves. (2) No host. Removal is an epoch advance at the room's host; without one there is nowhere to advance, and a local-only removal would seal to keys no other member holds. (3) A member that is not a DID. A leaf identifies a party by DID; a name identifies nobody the group knows. (4) An unbounded reason. Free text carried to another party is bounded (SPEC §7.3 item 19). (5) Bare/unnamespaced ext key — SPEC §4.5.1 requires every immediate child of ext to be reverse-DNS namespaced.

payload.invalid-examples.json of https://trusttasks.org/spec/rooms/records/put/0.2: (1) Two blobs on one record. A record carries at most one file in 0.2; `blobs` is an array so that several is a later minor version, not something a host may accept today without a sealed body that can describe more than one file. (2) An empty `blobs` array. A record with no file omits the member; an empty array would be a second spelling of absence that a host and a producer could disagree about when deciding whether a rewrite releases the previous version's blob. (3) A blob named by a bare hex SHA-256 rather than a multibase multihash. A BlobRef is self-describing so that the hash can change
